input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) bars any assignment without the other party's consent, with no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent, and Section 3(c) separately prohibits Sparkling from assigning the Agreement at all absent Garman's written authorisation. That fails the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice; other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld) and, as to Section 3(c), approaches walk-away territory (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out). There is no change-of-control clause anywhere in the Agreement, so Garman has no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. We therefore edited Section 20(d) to the fallback formulation and deleted the conflicting assignment words from Section 3(c) so the clauses read consistently.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Mutual successor assignment on written notice; other assignments need consent not unreasonably withheld
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made assignment mutual for successors on written notice, with consent for any other assignment not to be unreasonably withheld, and removed the conflicting assignment restriction in Section 3(c) so the two clauses read consistently. This sits at our fallback position.
